text: Hi, welcome. This is a 15-minute recorded viva; everyone gets the same structure. To start: tell me about a project you built.

I built a job-matching web app saath a React frontend and a FastAPI backend on PostgreSQL. It parses resumes, ranks listings by skill overlap, aur I deployed woh on a small VPS. The hardest part was ek slow ranking query that I fixed by adding an indeks and caching results, which cut response time from about two seconds to under two hundred milliseconds.
Can you explain how a hash table works?

ek hash teybul runs the key through a hesh function to get an array indeks. Two keys can land on the same indeks, so you handle collisions, either by chaining saath a linked list per bucket or by open addressing with probing. Lookup is O(1) par average. When yeh load factor gets too high you resize and rehash, otherwise chains get long and woh degrades toward par).
What does Big-O notation tell us, and why do we care about it?

Big-O describes an upper bound on how an algorithm's running time or memory grows as yeh input size grows. It ignores constants and lower-order terms, so it lets us compare algorithms independent of hardware. For example, ek binary search at O(log n) will beat a linear scan at par) once the data is large, even if the scan is faster par tiny inputs.
What is an index in a database and what is the trade-off of adding one?

An index is an extra structure, usually a B-tree, that lets the deytabeys find rows without scanning the whole table, so reads on that column get much faster. The trade-off hai extra storage aur slower writes, since every insert or update must bhi update the index. So you indeks columns that appear in frequent WHERE or JOIN clauses, not everything.
What happens between typing a URL in a browser and seeing the page?

yeh browser first resolves the domain through DNS to get an IP address. Then it opens a TCP connection and does ek TLS handshake liye HTTPS. It sends an HTTP request, the server responds with HTML, aur the browser parses it, fetches CSS, JavaScript and images, builds the DOM, and renders yeh page.
What is the difference between a process and a thread?

ek process has its own memory space and is isolated from others, while threads inside ek prosess share yeh same memory. Threads are cheaper ko create and switch between, and sharing memory makes communication easy, but woh also causes race conditions, so you need locks or other synchronization. Processes are safer kyunki a crash mein one does not take down yeh others.
Your API was fast yesterday and today responses take ten seconds. Walk me through how you would find the cause.

pehle I would dekhta what changed, recent deploys or config changes. Then look at logs aur metrics to see where the time goes, and isolate whether it hai the database, yeh application code or the network, liye example by timing a slow query directly. Once I find the slow component I karunga reproduce it, fix it, and add monitoring so hum catch it earlier next time.
You need to build a URL shortener. How would you design it?

I would generate ek short unique id, for example ek base62 encoding ka an auto-increment counter or a random id with ek kolizhan check, aur store the mapping from id ko long URL mein a database. yeh redirect path must be fast, toh I would put a cache like Redis in front for hot links. Reads far outnumber writes, so I would scale reads with replicas aur caching.
Thank you, that's the end of the viva.
